metadata.name: curl
metadata.description: Transfer data to or from a server using various protocols

installation.note: curl is installed by default on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: curl (client URL) transfers data to or from servers using various protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, etc.). It's more powerful than wget - supports more protocols, can send data (POST requests), handle authentication, and is commonly used for API testing and web development.

syntax.description: Transfer data from or to URL. By default, curl outputs to stdout. Use -o to save to file.

options.description: Save output to file with remote filename

options.use_case: Save output to file with custom name

options.description: Specify HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.)
options.use_case: Send POST, PUT, DELETE requests (default is GET)
Send form data or JSON in POST request
Show HTTP status code or other transfer info

misconceptions.title: curl only downloads files
misconceptions.reality: curl can send data (POST, PUT), set headers, handle authentication, and work with many protocols. It's a full HTTP client, not just a downloader.
misconceptions.tip: curl is a full HTTP client - can send GET, POST, PUT, DELETE requests, set headers, send data. Much more than just downloading.

misconceptions.title: curl and wget are identical
misconceptions.misconception: curl and wget work the same way
misconceptions.reality: curl outputs to stdout by default (use -O to save), supports more protocols, can send data. wget saves to file by default, simpler for downloads.
misconceptions.tip: curl = outputs to stdout (use -O to save), more features. wget = saves to file, simpler. Use curl for APIs, wget for simple downloads.

common_pitfalls.description: curl outputs to stdout by default, not file
common_pitfalls.solution: Use curl -O to save with original name, or curl -o filename to save with custom name. Without these, output goes to terminal.

common_pitfalls.description: curl doesn't follow redirects by default
common_pitfalls.solution: Use curl -L to follow HTTP redirects automatically. Many URLs redirect, so -L is often needed.

related_commands.relationship: Download tool; curl for APIs/advanced, wget for simple downloads
related_commands.description: Download files from web (simpler than curl for basic downloads)

best_practices: Use curl -O to save files with original name
Use curl for API testing and development
Pipe JSON to jq for pretty printing: curl ... | jq
performance_tips: Use -s for scripts to suppress progress output
curl handles compression automatically when supported

additional_notes.default_behavior: curl outputs to stdout by default - use -O or -o to save to file
additional_notes.vs_wget: curl = outputs to stdout, more features, better for APIs. wget = saves to file, simpler, better for downloads.
additional_notes.api_testing: curl is excellent for API testing - can send any HTTP method, headers, data
additional_notes.common_patterns: Common: curl URL (view), curl -O URL (download), curl -X POST -d data URL (POST), curl -L URL (follow redirects)
